Uncloud v0.4.40 adds automatic 2× image enhancement across Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon and Linux x64.

- Generate, Edit and Product finish rendering, preserve the original, and automatically create and display an enlarged PNG. Automatic 2× enhancement is on by default and can be turned off. It never changes the generation model, encoder, prompt, adapters, seed, steps, guidance or selected rendering dimensions.
- Enhancement runs inside the image job and survives leaving the screen or backgrounding a connected browser. Jobs run sequentially. Progress and elapsed time include enhancement, and completion is reported after both stages finish.
- The viewer compares Original and Enhanced 2× without enhancing the result twice. Save and download use the displayed result. An enhancement failure or cancellation retains the completed original with an explanation.
- First use downloads a separately verified 64 MB Real-ESRGAN x2plus model through Uncloud's existing install approval. It then works offline. Pixel enhancement includes no added content classifier, face restoration or generation filter. Licenses and attribution ship with every installer.
- Manual Enhance 2× remains available in image viewers, including Outputs. Generation progress distinguishes model loading, prompt processing, rendering, decoding and saving. Completed MLX jobs release their progress callbacks while keeping model weights resident.

Measured on a 24 GiB Apple silicon Mac with Klein 4B 8-bit MLX: a matched 2048×1536 example took 88.2 seconds when rendered directly, versus 39.0 seconds of processing for 1024×768 generation followed by 2× enhancement. Those manual-stage timings exclude time between clicks. This is a different larger-image workflow, not a general native-resolution diffusion speedup; reconstructed detail differs from native larger rendering. Performance and quality vary by model, image and device. The original is always preserved.

Verification covers the generation and edit pipeline, all supported engine dispatch paths, sequential work, opt-out, stopping/failure fallback, first-use approval, authenticated original/result retrieval, viewer comparison and production web packaging. Native GPU image quality and timing were tested on macOS; Windows/Linux inference performance requires validation on those machines. The release workflow builds and verifies all three installers before publication.
